A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NRGBoost research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original inference and synthetic-data experiments on seven datasets, along with training-time and MCMC analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds probabilistic prediction, missing-covariate inference, challenging-dataset, and sampling-time results.

M1.justification: The second-order boosting objective, tree construction, line search, regularization, amortized sampling, and DEF ensemble construction remain unchanged. The new diagram and Algorithm 1 document the existing procedure; the PDFs do not establish an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original datasets and adds ALOI classification restricted to 250 classes and Microsoft regression with 1.2 million examples and 136 features. Appendix E.3 also adds missing-covariate test scenarios on California Housing, Adult, and Covertype, substantially extending evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: NGBoost changes from a cited alternative to an evaluated regression baseline in Tables 1 and 11. Table 12 adds XGBoost with mean, median/mode, and five-neighbor imputation. The MNIST sample montage drops DEF (KL), although its quantitative comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include MAE and (C)RPS evaluation, median-based predictions, removal of specified test covariates, NGBoost tuning, manually tuned Microsoft experiments, and timing 10,000 independent samples. v2 also specifies an Adult DEF leaf cap of 8,192 instead of the 16,384 listed in v1. This reported setting revision does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds missing-feature robustness tests, analysis of probabilistic forecasts and mean-versus-median predictions, and sampling-efficiency analysis including the reported similarity of results with 30 versus 100 Gibbs iterations. The existing MNIST chain-convergence analysis is retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The retained experiments use the same five-fold or five-synthetic-dataset repetitions, standard errors, and 95% t-test conventions. Table 11 follows the existing reporting practice. Its predictive-distribution evaluation does not introduce a new procedure for estimating uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and the relocated Wasserstein tables are unchanged. New results cover NGBoost, probabilistic forecasts, missing covariates, challenging datasets, and sampling time. Table 13 reports NRGBoost/XGBoost accuracy of 0.962/0.943 on restricted ALOI and RMSE of 0.787/0.744 on Microsoft; Table 14 reports TabDDPM sampling 9.67 times faster in the median case.

T1.justification: The derivations and likelihood-increase bound remain essentially unchanged; renaming Appendix A.2 does not introduce a new convergence proof. However, the relocated DET sampling statement changes leaf-selection probabilities from empirical leaf masses in v1 Section 4 to density values v_j in v2 Appendix B. Since its normalization uses v_j times leaf volume, this introduces a localized mathematical inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: second-order generative boosting, amortized sampling, and bagged density-estimation trees, with competitive inference and sampling performance. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations involving nonparametric forecast flexibility and missing-data marginalization, plus substantive discussion of sampling bias, computational tradeoffs, cardinality limits, and impractical tuning on Microsoft. It also discusses arbitrary conditional sampling as an unexplored advantage. Conversely, v1's explicit full-training-data memory limitation is removed.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a repository address where v1 referred to supplementary code and promised an open-source library. It adds training pseudocode, toy-distribution parameters, NGBoost search details, Microsoft settings, and mentions Numba and Linux. Most existing implementation, hardware, and reproducibility information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds comparisons with TabPFN-based energy models and McCarter's autoregressive tree approach, and correctly describes Forest-Flow as conditional flow matching. It removes v1's explicit claim that bagged DET ensembles had not previously been explored. The central positioning against earlier generative boosting remains intact.

P1.justification: Editing extends throughout the paper. The standalone DET/DEF section is consolidated into related work and Appendix B, Wasserstein material moves to Appendix E.1, and the discussion, tuning descriptions, and appendix organization are substantially revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds a training-loop diagram, Algorithm 1, and five new tables. It relocates and reformats the MNIST montage, removes its DEF panel, redraws the California visualizations, and moves the Wasserstein tables to the appendix. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the density model's practical advantages: Tables 11–12 directly test probabilistic predictions and missing-feature inference, which v1 largely motivated conceptually. Challenging-dataset results and measured sampling costs also clarify applicability and weaknesses. Clearer algorithm documentation and code-access information help reproducibility. These gains outweigh the localized DET sampling inconsistency and removal of the memory limitation.
